status: CANDIDATE_PENDING_LLM_CONSENSUS (P4-A, SDK#484; selection rule v2: governance anchors vs adjacent references)
unit: one fixed-scope engagement = one action (candidate mapping)
assessment_scope: StegVerse governance starter: authority map, risk matrix, five prioritized remediations, 30-day plan (Labs #3370). scope_match records, per comparable, how each published deliverable list maps onto that scope; no comparable matches it exactly.
selection_rule: GOVERNANCE_ANCHOR: a price published in USD on the vendor's own page for a fixed-scope AI governance or AI-management-system assessment of a small organization that delivers a written inventory or gap analysis plus a prioritized plan and carries explicit governance content (authority, policy, controls). ADJACENT_REFERENCE: a verified adjacent-market price (e.g. AI adoption readiness) kept as context; never enters the median. Excluded entirely: self-serve questionnaires and automated reports; single-workflow briefs and single sessions; reference or 'typical' values; non-USD prices; enterprise programs at $12,500 or more.
anchor_note: Three governance anchors now exist (Continuous $1,995 flat; Veracity AI $8,000-$12,000 range; Certify $9,750 fixed), with different depth, environment and credit conditions, and Veracity's deliverables are not itemized. The engine reads the range as bounds: the median is a range, not a point, and the price is positioned at its lower bound. The tier stays PROVISIONAL_SCENARIO and quote_ready false while the cost basis is a machine-only subtotal.
price_basis_note: The engine reads a STARTING_AT price p as a lower bound (the true price is at least p): the market median is reported as a range, a STARTING_AT figure never counts as an exact match, and it never caps a quote.
citation_check: Each source page was fetched and its price, scope and duration checked by hand on observed_at. The guard test checks only citation form.
not_included_note: northsecure.ai (a Microsoft 365 security assessment priced in CAD) and aidigitalhub.com (priced in INR) were never part of this set. The currency rule excludes them.
